title: Teluni Identity Provider Evaluation
html:
Selected policies · PH-11 · ADR-0024 decision

Evaluation scope and result

On 2026-10-18, the owner selected self-hosting and Keycloak, then explicitly approved all pending Teluni ADRs, including ADR-0024/ADR-0025. Host feasibility and actual integration qualification remain delivery prerequisites. No recurring identity/email procurement budget is available. This is a documentation/source review, not a deployed-provider experiment, security assessment or proof of operational capacity. Keycloak 26.8.1, release published on 2026-10-13, was inspected at source commit 24ed1dadf3f246a555adb6d3d4a99e9b3003fb3b for the assessment below. This pins review evidence only; no deployment image/digest has been selected or installed. Reassess the deployment version and security status before implementation; mutable latest documentation does not pin a production dependency.

The existing verifier and accepted ADR-0012 are the executable/governing boundary. Do not weaken it because a candidate emits different defaults. The source/documentation review and explicit owner approval satisfy PH-11's architectural decision scope. They do not qualify a running integration. Required policies and measured bounds remain in the identity policy, not vendor defaults.

Evidence and remaining qualification

Concern Evidence available Required qualification before integration/readiness claims
typ=at+jwt Official release notes document an explicit client setting, disabled by default Pin a maintained compatible version, enable the setting and verify a real synthetic-user access token; do not substitute an ID token or accept default JWT headers
Signature, issuer, API audience and JWKS OIDC integration documentation and protocol mappers provide integration primitives Confirm exact issuer/audience/JWKS, allowed RS256/ES256 signing and rotation, required sub/iat/exp/scope, and wrong-environment/audience rejection through the unchanged verifier
Stable application principal and human assertion Attribute/hardcoded mapping primitives are documented; the repository requires orion_principal_id and orion_actor_type=human Specify trusted provisioning/immutable principal mapping and human-only client/flow restrictions; prove users cannot self-edit privileged attributes or issue accepted machine tokens with a hardcoded human assertion
Google, credentials and assurance The administration guide documents Google brokering, passkeys, authenticators and recovery capabilities Qualify selected-version maturity, proven linking, email trust, assurance/recency mapping, non-bypassable privileged flows, and recovery/session invalidation; do not assume every Google/passkey login satisfies MFA
Browser sessions and refresh Provider protocols supply a basis; the current web shell has only in-memory bearer handling Apply accepted ADR-0024 and review the concrete trusted session linkage; qualify server token storage, cookie/CSRF controls, logout/refresh replay/concurrency and selected idle/absolute/session-count bounds. No session library is chosen
Application authorization and revocation Existing verification returns principal ID/scopes only; no product membership/session store exists Apply accepted ADR-0025 and review the required adapter/context changes; prove 30-second account/session/membership revocation and current-state sensitive confirmation. JWT expiry is insufficient
Hosting and recovery The official container guide describes production setup and recommends a 2 GB container memory limit for small production-ready deployments PH-10 must measure total host headroom, durable provider state, restricted management, patching, backup and isolated restore. That recommendation is not a measured Teluni capacity result
Mail, external accounts and portability Capabilities exist, but no Teluni sender, Google OAuth client or deployment is verified PH-15–PH-17 must supply controlled resources/configuration and safe evidence; Completed PH-12 policies define public commercial access; PH-13/PH-18/PH-19 retain applicable actual readiness. Assess migration limits without adding P37=B's unselected mandatory pre-pilot export/import proof

The orion_* claim names are an inherited application contract, not a demand to rebrand them or use Keycloak subjects as application IDs. Mapping a UUID-looking user-editable attribute is insufficient. Pin principal creation, authoritative ownership, (issuer, subject) association, uniqueness and migration semantics during design. Do not add machine-client grants to a human client and assume a hardcoded actor mapper distinguishes them. Provider roles may inform trusted mapping but cannot replace current application memberships/resource permissions.

Pinned-source assessment

Evidence was read from the official 26.8.1 release and the immutable source commit above. Nine Java source files were downloaded outside the repository for inspection; no downloaded code was executed, provider started or token issued. This is a supported architectural compatibility assessment, not an interoperability test.

Existing API requirement Pinned-source evidence / accepted integration responsibility
Exact typ=at+jwt DefaultTokenManager selects the RFC 9068 access-token header when the client option is enabled; OIDCConfigAttributes defines access.token.header.type.rfc9068. Configure it explicitly; do not change the existing verifier's accepted type
Signed tokens and exact issuer/audience The signing path in DefaultTokenManager uses the configured signature provider. TokenManager sets issuer; SubMapper supplies the persistent user subject; AudienceProtocolMapper adds the configured audience. The integration must select RS256 or ES256 and the exact trusted API issuer/audience/JWKS, then test actual signatures/key rotation and denial cases
sub, iat, exp, string scope TokenManager initializes access tokens from the authenticated user/session and sets the scope string; AccessToken and JsonWebToken define their representation/time lifecycle. Actual emitted types, clock bounds and expiry remain verifier integration tests
Application principal UUID UserAttributeMapper maps a configured user attribute into a configured token claim. Trusted provisioning must generate an application UUID, keep a unique stable (issuer, subject) association and map a non-user-editable attribute to orion_principal_id. User profile edits, signup, Google imports and tenant administrators cannot create/replace that attribute; fail closed until the trusted mapping exists
Trusted human assertion HardcodedClaim can supply orion_actor_type=human only in a restricted human-login client/flow. Disable service-account, password/direct-grant and unreviewed exchange/impersonation paths on that client; a constant mapper alone does not prove a human. Test that machine credentials cannot produce an accepted human token
Session/assurance freshness The current verifier deliberately returns only principal/scopes. The reviewed OIDC boundary must bind verified login assertions and current server session/assurance state to that principal and the legitimate access token. An ID token may establish login context at its intended OIDC boundary but never substitutes for the API access token. Enforce the 30-second session/membership revocation goal using application state, not unimplemented claims or provider logout alone

The review found a viable standards-based mapping path without changing ADR-0012. It does not assert that a default Keycloak client/token already meets the contract. Immutable principal provisioning, protected profile attributes, human-only flow restrictions and trusted session/assurance binding are mandatory implementation design/control requirements under PJ-07/PJ-24, not controls that were deployed in this task. Deployment version/image selection remains PH-15/PJ-24.

Alternatives and tradeoffs

Direction Assessment for the current decision
Self-hosted Keycloak Owner-approved provider; operational control with responsibility for resources, upgrades, mail and recovery. Documentation indicates relevant primitives; integration remains unqualified
Managed established OIDC provider Could reduce some hosting responsibilities, but recurring cost, limits, claim compatibility and migration would need a new evaluation. No vendor price/free-tier comparison or rejection on unsupported cost claims is asserted
Another established self-hosted provider Remains a fallback if Keycloak cannot meet required compatibility/operations. No comparative benchmark has been performed; a provider change after acceptance requires a new reviewed decision
API-owned passwords, home-grown issuer or weakened JWT checks Not an acceptable shortcut under inherited authentication policy/ADR-0012

The owner also selected server-managed browser sessions over a browser-token SPA direction. This keeps provider credentials off browser JavaScript but adds session persistence, CSRF defenses and lifecycle/revocation work. It can compose into the modular backend; it neither mandates a new service nor changes the client-first web architecture to server rendering.

Decision completion and remaining delivery gates

  1. Completed: 38 direct owner policy answers, the default/custom scoped matrix, IA-01–IA-16 specified allow/deny cases, explicit acceptance of ADR-0024/ADR-0025 and the pinned-source compatibility assessment. PH-11 is completed for provider/policy/architecture selection.
  2. Pending implementation: concrete session/assurance contracts, principal provisioning, runtime claim configuration and every actual token/login/refresh/revocation/recovery test under PJ-03/PJ-24. New contract or mechanism choices still follow the normal design/ADR process where significant.
  3. Pending external/readiness evidence: PH-15–PH-17 identity/Google/mail resources, PH-10/PJ-13 capacity and restore, completed PH-12 policy and PH-13/PH-18/PH-19 public/paid-activation evidence and real release acceptance. No finished decision silently satisfies these gates.

No provider provisioning, test login, email delivery, Google callback, token interoperability, session revocation, MFA recovery or restore was performed in this documentation task. Foundation pnpm validate cannot qualify those future flows. PH-11 is completed for the human architectural decision. Actual provider/session qualification remains PJ-24, and external readiness remains PH-15–PH-17; neither is reported as passed.
